title: Jev-LiteMAS: Separating Decisions from Generation in Multi-Agent Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2610.21411v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on generative models for expert execution, workflow planning, and artifact review. Yet many coordination operations require only bounded decisions, such as selecting the next expert or judging artifact quality. Profiling three representative MAS frameworks, we find that routing and review account for 31.7-43.5% of generative-LLM tokens. However, replacing these operations with low-cost decision models introduces two interface gaps: generative planners produce execution plans and handoff instructions (planning gap), while reviewers provide actionable feedback for repairing flawed artifacts (review gap), which bounded decisions alone cannot provide. We introduce Jev-LiteMAS, a multi-agent framework that bridges both gaps by combining a lightweight decision model (Jev) with generative execution and feedback. translated_title: Jev-LiteMAS：在多智能体工作流中分离决策与生成
translated_abstract: 多智能体大语言模型系统依赖生成式模型来执行专家任务、工作流规划和产物评审。然而，许多协调操作只需要有界决策，例如选择下一个专家或判断产物质量。通过对三个代表性多智能体系统框架进行性能分析，我们发现路由和评审操作占生成式LLM token消耗的31.7%至43.5%。然而，用低成本决策模型替换这些操作会引入两个接口鸿沟：生成式规划器会产生执行计划和交接指令（规划鸿沟），而评审器会为修复有缺陷的产物提供可操作的反馈（评审鸿沟），这些是有界决策本身无法提供的。我们提出了Jev-LiteMAS，这是一个通过将轻量级决策模型与生成式执行和反馈相结合来弥合这两个鸿沟的多智能体框架。为解决规划鸿沟，Jev根据任务和先前专家的输出动态选择专家，使用……
tldr: 该论文提出Jev-LiteMAS框架，通过将轻量级决策模型与生成式执行和反馈相结合，在多智能体系统中分离决策与生成功能，在显著降低路由和评审环节token开销（原占31.7%-43.5%）的同时弥合了规划鸿沟与评审鸿沟。
en_tdlr: Jev-LiteMAS is a multi-agent framework that separates bounded decision-making from generation by combining a lightweight decision model with generative execution and feedback, cutting routing and review token costs (originally 31.7-43.5%) while bridging both the planning and review gaps.
